subject: Post-call recap: BrightCart usage profile, burst economics & quota path
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightcart.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: BrightCart usage profile, burst economics & quota path

Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. TL;DR: BrightCart baseline ~5M tokens/mo, expected event spikes during peak promotions (multi-day) up to ~30M tokens over 48h; you asked about how Redwood handles burst limits, quota increases, and what a target $/1M tokens would look like for a pilot.

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Current baseline: ~5,000,000 tokens/month (search + recommendation NLG).
- Typical steady QPS: ~6 req/sec with 250-400 tokens/req.
- Expected peak windows: concentrated around marketing events (2–4 hour peaks historically, but Black Friday-like events can generate multi-day sustained load). You estimated a 48-hour peak that could materialize as ~30M tokens total during the event.
- Budget signal: pilot budget range you mentioned on call: $20k–$75k/month depending on SLA and burst safety net.

Our preliminary commercial framing
- Target unit we discussed: $/1M tokens. For the pilot we can look at a stepped rate depending on committed baseline and burst allowance. Ballpark target for conversation: $900–$1,100 per 1M tokens depending on committed baseline and burst guardrails.
- Burst approach: soft quota + controlled overage tiers. We typically offer a negotiated burst allowance (e.g., 3x baseline for short windows) and then overage priced in tiers to avoid sticker shock.

Questions we need answered (please confirm by EOD Mon):
1) Confirm monthly baseline (you said ~5M — please confirm).
2) For peak events: are spikes usually concentrated (hours) or sustained (days)? We need a distribution to size burst allowance correctly.
3) Target SLA for production (p95 latency, required availability).
4) Any data residency / PII concerns for these requests?

Proposed immediate next steps (what I can do now)
- Internal price sketch for pilot (include 1M token unit price options and overage tiers) — Ben to draft.
- Draft mutual action plan (MAP) for pilot timeline + success metrics — I’ll share a first draft (attached).
- If you want a quota jump ahead of the MAP, we can provide a temporary burst allowance while the pilot contract is processed (need written confirmation of expected event window).

Attachments: BrightCart_call_notes.pdf (summary + rough token profile), BC_token_profile.csv (raw usage buckets), RDW-MAP-draft.docx (pilot MAP).

Thanks — Neha

Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below and one ask.

Confirmed: baseline is 5M tokens/month (avg). The 30M number is our high-case for a 48-hour campaign (two large promo pushes + downstream churn). Historically spikes skew heavy within 4–6 hour windows, but marketing told me Black Friday last year had sustained elevated usage over ~36 hours.

Budget: we are flexible for the pilot — can go up to $75k for a short-term pilot if we get predictable burst handling and conservative cost guardrails. If we start smaller we'll be around $25k/month.

Question: what is your operational process for urgent quota increases? Suppose we see an unplanned surge tomorrow and need +4x tokens for 12 hours — how fast can Redwood raise the quota and how will the overage be billed?

Also — can you share an example overage tier table and a simple example invoice calc? We need to show this to procurement.

Happy to sync 30m Monday if helpful.

—Sam

BrightCart

Looping in high-level commercial thinking for the MAP and procurement ask.

Proposed pilot pricing sketch (internal to RDW) — rough, subject to negs:
- Committed baseline: 5M tokens/mo at $850 per 1M tokens (monthly committed billing).
- Pilot burst allowance: up to an additional 7.5M tokens usable across 30 days at no incremental charge (to validate traffic patterns) OR a short-term trial burst: 3x baseline for the first 7 days of pilot.
- Overage tiers beyond burst allowance: Tier A (0–10M over burst): $1,000 / 1M tokens; Tier B (10–50M over burst): $900 / 1M tokens; Tier C (50M+): $750 / 1M tokens (volume discount).

Operational process for quota increases:
- Standard: self-service quota requests (via Console) with automated checks; typical automated bump within 15–30 minutes for non-critical increases (if safety checks pass).
- For urgent increases (unplanned surge): 24/7 ops channel escalation to our capacity team. We can approve temporary soft-burst in under 60 minutes if key contacts confirm the window and we have capacity. Formal, sustained permanent quota increases require signed MAP + PO (3–5 business days).

Billing example (simple)
- Baseline 5M @ $850/1M = $4,250/month.
- If pilot used 12M tokens in a month (7M over baseline) and pilot burst allowance covers 3.75M free: remaining 3.25M billed in Tier A at $1,000/1M => $3,250. Total = $7,500 for month.

I recommend we offer a one-time courtesy burst buffer for the first scheduled promo as part of onboarding (helps reduce procurement friction). Neha — can you include this in the MAP and make an explicit clause about emergency quota process and ticket SLAs?

Ben
VP, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — noted. Sam, attached is a first-draft MAP (RDW-MAP-draft.docx) that captures the timeline, pilot metrics, and the commercial sketch Ben proposed. Highlights from MAP:
- Onboarding week (week 0): confirm baseline metrics, attach test tokens, set up Console alerts.
- Pilot period (30 days): committed baseline 5M tokens/mo; courtesy burst buffer: 7.5M tokens available during pilot (usable across pilot window).
- Emergency quota path: 24/7 ops channel + capacity-team escalation (target time to temporary approval: <=60 mins) — permanent increases require signed MAP + PO.
- Billing: baseline billed monthly; overage invoiced monthly with tiered pricing (example table included in doc).

Next immediate asks:
- Sam: Please confirm the pilot start week (your preferred start date) and whether you want the courtesy buffer applied to the first promo event or distributed across the 30-day pilot.
- Sam & procurement: I will attach a short, plain-language example invoice calc for your procurement team (Ben: can you provide a one-page calc we can attach?).

If you’re good with the MAP sketch I’ll upload the HubSpot deal (link included) and send the DocuSign for the pilot SOW with the commercial sketch. Proposed MAP deliverable timeline:
- EOD Mon: Confirm baseline and event distribution.
- Tue: HubSpot deal + DocuSign prep.
- Wed: Sign SOW (goal) -> Pilot kickoff next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m Monday to iron specifics.
